records.body:
Contains bounded Windows FFI, subprocess, Unicode and int128 backend repairs. **The Windows baseline remains unrepaired: both final-head full Windows jobs fail the repro-hash golden check.** PR base: `88300f14c1da1066ad6db25d31be0e8e912b3ef0`. Current correction head: **`cbb324ad41cb1503e6ae92710849adb97562ee25`**.

The latest correction starts from Gemini's `a189ff1b9f6bace9224a23810b78c533a63e33a2` and fixes capture creation: exclusive private objects, checked failures, retained handles/descriptors, safe partial cleanup, and no pathname reopening. Release-active regressions cover existing-file/symlink preservation, permissions, collision rejection, Unicode observed through Windows wmain, empty arguments, spaces, quotes/backslashes, shell metacharacters, cwd/environment, nonzero exits and simultaneous 2 MiB stdout/stderr. Windows reparse creation prints an explicit supported/skip outcome. CMake links advapi32 and the test thread dependency.

Final-head execution: **MSVC and clang-cl full builds succeed; both suites pass 403/404 and fail only repro-hash drift** (expected `ea52b9ed…`, actual `e13940b5…`; root cause unestablished). Both capture regressions pass, including executed file-symlink reparse rejection, private permissions/cleanup, Unicode observed through wmain, quoting/metacharacters and concurrent large output. macOS ARM64 CI passes 426/426; Linux ASan/UBSan CI passes 427/427. Local targeted Release tests pass 3/3, with standalone -DNDEBUG, ASan/UBSan and a failing negative control. Final-head CI format/docs/warning checks pass; AI status freshness fails on three unchanged documents; CodeQL remains in progress. Complete Windows job/artifact links and exact hash discrepancy are retained in the final evidence comment.

[Capture correction commands, logs and limits](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/tree/cbb324ad41cb1503e6ae92710849adb97562ee25/docs/records/audits/2026-11-13-pr782-secure-capture).

Historical negative evidence remains preserved: [5201421 complete Windows results](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/pull/782#issuecomment-6839556377) show both full builds completed but both jobs failed 401/403 on FFI/repro-hash; that is not a result for the current head. [Arithmetic correction record](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/tree/5201421142313036635791d8a8f32744fb8693ac/docs/records/audits/2026-11-12-pr782-int128-correction) preserves the clean-main macOS FFI/fixture failures and separate root-cause limits. Native Windows clang-cl signed __int128 linked unsuccessfully on missing __divti3; MSVC rejected the type; both selected portable 128-bit arithmetic. Those implementation/probe/test files remain unchanged by the capture correction.

The same Codex session authored the earlier arithmetic correction and latest capture repair; Gemini authored the intervening delta. These tests are regression evidence, not independent scientific validation. No universal arithmetic, production-readiness or comparative-performance claim follows. Generic capture has no child timeout or output cap; the regression target has a 60-second timeout. Windows sanitizers and unsupported reparse scenarios are not established by macOS execution. Earlier Release-disabled duplicate-registration asserts remain a separate pre-existing limit.

No #779/#780 changes, weakened checks, check bypasses, benchmark campaign, merge or SCG-08 advancement.

records.title: bench(core): establish BASE-PERF-00 correctness-verified Cell throughput baseline
records.head: a31b862e6bbdc7c136a74c9117aa085a13b4da2c
records.body:
# T81 BASE-PERF-00 — Correctness-Verified `Cell` Throughput Baseline

## Scope and Governance Notice

This record documents an authorized, bounded **BASE-PERF-00** engineering throughput baseline for `t81::core::Cell` (5-trit balanced ternary cell, range `[-121, +121]`) using the existing TCB-Core `benchmark_runner` infrastructure.

- **Not an SCG-08 Gate 2 experiment:** Does not execute SCG-08 measurement campaigns, modify SCG-08 historical evidence, or alter RFC-00E1 status (`DRAFT`, Gate 1 `WITHHELD`, Gate 2 `STRICT NO-GO`).
- **Unmodified production arithmetic:** `include/t81/types/cell.hpp` is completely untouched (`0` lines modified) so that these measurements establish an unoptimized-against-history engineering reference point.
- **Historical reports preserved:** `docs/reference/benchmarks.md` and `docs/reference/benchmarks_engineering.md` are unmodified.
- **No comparative superiority claims:** Binary comparative performance superiority is **NOT EVALUATED**.

---

## Phase A — Execution Identity

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Baseline `main` Commit SHA** | `d3a6cf55517a3098d7bae91b07c72694bc3472da` |
| **Host CPU** | Apple M2 (`machdep.cpu.brand_string: Apple M2`) |
| **Architecture** | `arm64` (`arm64-apple-darwin25.5.0`), 8 logical/physical cores (`hw.ncpu: 8`), L1D 64 KiB, L1I 128 KiB, L2 Unified 4 MiB |
| **System Memory** | 8 GiB (`hw.memsize: 8589934592`) |
| **Operating System / Kernel** | macOS 26.5.2 (Build `25F84`), Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0 (`RELEASE_ARM64_T8112`) |
| **Virtualization Check** | Physical host (`sysctl kern.hv_vmm_present = 0`, non-virtualized local developer workstation: MacBook Air M2; not a dedicated datacenter reference server) |
| **Compiler** | Apple clang version 21.0.0 (`clang-2100.1.1.101`, `/usr/bin/c++`) |
| **Build Configuration** | CMake 4.3 `Release` (`-O3 -DNDEBUG -std=gnu++23 -arch arm64 -fPIE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -DBENCHMARK_STATIC_DEFINE -DT81_DETERMINISTIC`) |
| **SIMD Compile Target** | `AVX2=0, SSE4.2=0, NEON=1` |
| **Benchmark Library** | Google Benchmark `v1.9.5` |
| **Real Arithmetic Verification** | Confirmed in `include/t81/types/cell.hpp`: `operator+` executes 5-trit balanced-ternary ripple-carry addition; `operator-` executes trit-wise negation plus ripple-carry addition; `operator*` executes 5-trit shift-and-add; `operator/` executes `to_int()`, `int64_t` division, and `from_int()`; `from_int` / `to_int` execute base-3 balanced-ternary conversion. |

---

## Phase B — Numerical Correctness Oracle Results

Correctness was validated against a host `int64_t` oracle in two places:
1. **Standalone CTest executable (`t81_determinism_primitives_test` in `tests/determinism/test_primitives.cpp`):** Exhaustively tests the full `Cell` state space (`[-121, +121]`, $3^5 = 243$ states, $243^2 = 59{,}049$ ordered pairs) plus the exact seeded benchmark input sequences.
2. **Untimed prevalidation phase inside `arith_throughput.cpp` and `roundtrip_accuracy.cpp`:** Prevalidates all $10{,}000$ deterministic inputs and boundary/exception conditions before any timed loop executes. If prevalidation fails, the benchmark aborts via `state.SkipWithError(...)`.

| Operation / Check | Tested Domain | Oracle Result | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Conversion Round-Trip (`from_int` / `to_int`)** | Exhaustive `[-121, +121]` + out-of-range `{-10000, -243, -122, +122, +243, +10000}` | **PASS** (`243 / 243` exact; `6 / 6` out-of-range throw `std::overflow_error`) | Bijective round-trip, canonical trit uniqueness, strict ordering (`prev < c`), and involution (`-(-c) == c`). |
| **Addition (`operator+`)** | Exhaustive `[-121, +121]^2` (`59,049` pairs) | **PASS** (`0` mismatches) | `44,287` in-range pairs match `int64_t` `a + b` exactly; all `14,762` pairs with `|a + b| > 121` deterministically throw `std::overflow_error`. |
| **Subtraction (`operator-`)** | Exhaustive `[-121, +121]^2` (`59,049` pairs) | **PASS** (`0` mismatches) | `44,287` in-range pairs match `int64_t` `a - b` exactly; all `14,762` pairs with `|a - b| > 121` deterministically throw `std::overflow_error`. |
| **Multiplication (`operator*`) — Benchmark Domain** | Exhaustive `[-10, +10]^2` (`441` pairs) | **PASS** (`441 / 441` exact, `0` exceptions) | All products in `[-10, +10]^2` lie in `[-100, +100]` and fit in the lower 3 trits (`1 + 3 + 9 = 13 >= 10`), so no intermediate shift or partial sum overflows. |
| **Multiplication (`operator*`) — Full Domain Characterization** | Exhaustive `[-121, +121]^2` (`59,049` pairs) | **PASS** (`0` silent corruptions) | `2,553` pairs succeed and match `int64_t` `a * b` exactly; `56,144` pairs with `|a * b| > 121` throw `std::overflow_error`; `352` pairs with `|a * b| <= 121` throw `std::overflow_error` due to intermediate 5-trit shift (`*this << i`) or partial-sum overflow (documented limitation below). |
| **Division (`operator/`)** | Exhaustive `[-121, +121]^2` (`59,049` pairs) | **PASS** (`0` mismatches) | All `58,806` pairs with `b != 0` match C++ truncated `int64_t` division `a / b`; all `243` pairs with `b == 0` deterministically throw `std::domain_error`. |
| **Seeded Timed Workload Prevalidation** | `std::mt19937_64(0x781)`, `DATA_SIZE = 10,000` | **PASS** (`0` failures across `50,000` prevalidated operations) | Arithmetic pairs in `[-10, +10]` (`val_b == 0 -> 1`) and conversion inputs in `[-121, +121]` prevalidated before timing. |

---

## Phase C — Measurement-Blocking Defects Repaired

1. **Separated per-operation measurement & exception accounting (`benchmarks/runner/arith_throughput.cpp`):**
   - Previously, `BM_ArithThroughput_T81Cell` bundled `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/` in a single loop and caught `std::exception` with `continue` while unconditionally reporting `state.SetItemsProcessed(state.iterations() * DATA_SIZE * 4)`.
   - Added dedicated 5-repetition benchmarks (`BM_CellAdd_T81Cell`, `BM_CellSub_T81Cell`, `BM_CellMul_T81Cell`, `BM_CellDiv_T81Cell`), prevalidated inputs before timing, tracked `completed_ops` and `failed_ops` explicitly, and called `state.SkipWithError(...)` if `failed_ops > 0`.
   - Explicitly labeled `BM_CellDiv_T81Cell` with `semantics=to_int+int64_div+from_int` and `convs_per_op=3` because `Cell::operator/` converts operands via `to_int()`, divides in `int64_t`, and converts back via `from_int()`.
2. **Compiler dead-code / `constexpr`-folding prevention & untimed oracle separation (`benchmarks/runner/roundtrip_accuracy.cpp`):**
   - Previously, `BM_RoundtripAccuracy_T81Cell` evaluated `if (Cell::from_int(val).to_int() == val)` inside the timed loop without `DoNotOptimize` barriers on the input `int64_t`, intermediate `Cell`, or output `int64_t`.
   - Added `BM_CellRoundtrip_T81Cell` (and updated `BM_RoundtripAccuracy_T81Cell`) with untimed oracle prevalidation and explicit `DoNotOptimize(val)`, `DoNotOptimize(cell)`, `DoNotOptimize(roundtrip)`, and `ClobberMemory()` barriers inside the timed loop.
3. **Per-repetition retention and median aggregation (`benchmarks/runner/benchmark_runner.cpp`):**
   - Previously, `CustomReporter::ReportRuns` overwrote `final_results[family]` on each `RT_Iteration` repetition, losing earlier repetitions and reporting only the final repetition.
   - `BenchmarkResult` now retains all per-repetition throughput and latency values, computes the **median** across repetitions (`ComputeMedian`), and reports per-repetition raw values, median, min, max, range, standard deviation, and CV% when `T81_BENCHMARK_VERBOSE_CONSOLE=1` is set.
4. **Removal of unsupported `apples-to-apples` claims (`benchmarks/runner/arith_throughput.cpp`, `benchmarks/runner/benchmark_runner.cpp`):**
   - Removed `comparison=apples-to-apples` from `arith_throughput.cpp` (`comparison=not-evaluated`) and updated `FairnessFor` / `UserRow` in `benchmark_runner.cpp` so benchmarks labeled `comparison=not-evaluated` or `comparison=semantic-tax` are never classified as `"apples-to-apples"` or assigned comparative win/loss verdicts.

---

## Phase D — Bounded Measurement Results (HOST-LOCAL / PHYSICAL WORKSTATION)

### Exact Build and Execution Commands

```bash
# 1. Configure Release build (using local Google Benchmark v1.9.5 source cache)
cmake -S . -B build-release \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DT81_BUILD_TUI=OFF \
  -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_GOOGLEBENCHMARK=/Users/t81dev/Code/t81-foundation/build/_deps/googlebenchmark-src \
  -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_ASIO=/Users/t81dev/Code/t81-foundation/build/_deps/asio-src

# 2. Build correctness test and benchmark_runner
cmake --build build-release --target t81_determinism_primitives_test benchmark_runner -j4

# 3. Execute exhaustive host-integer oracle correctness test
./build-release/t81_determinism_primitives_test

# 4. Execute bounded BASE-PERF-00 benchmark (5 repetitions per operation after 0.05s warmup)
T81_BENCHMARK_VERBOSE_CONSOLE=1 T81_BENCHMARK_WRITE_REPORTS=0 \
  ./build-release/benchmarks/benchmark_runner \
  --benchmark_filter='^BM_Cell(Add|Sub|Mul|Div|Roundtrip)_T81Cell' \
  --benchmark_min_warmup_time=0.05 \
  --benchmark_min_time=0.05s \
  --benchmark_out=docs/benchmarks/base_perf_00_cell_throughput_raw.json \
  --benchmark_out_format=json
```

---

## Limitations and Unresolved Technical Findings

1. **Conversion-backed `Cell::operator/`:**
   - Despite the source comment in `include/t81/types/cell.hpp` (`Division (restoring division, exact when divisible)`), `Cell::operator/` actually converts both `Cell` operands to `int64_t` via `to_int()`, performs host integer division `a / b`, and converts back via `Cell::from_int(a / b)`. Consequently, `BM_CellDiv_T81Cell` measures a hybrid conversion + host-division path (`3` conversions per division), not a native balanced-ternary restoring division algorithm.
2. **Intermediate shift overflow in `Cell::operator*` outside `[-13, +13]`:**
   - `Cell::operator*` computes `*this << i` into a 5-trit `Cell` before adding or subtracting into the running 5-trit accumulator. When the multiplicand uses trit 3 or 4 (`|a| > 13`) and the multiplier has non-zero trits at index `i >= 1` that cancel down into range (e.g., `50 * 2 = 100`, where `2 = 3 - 1`), `*this << 1` (`150 > 121`) throws `std::overflow_error("Shift overflow (non-zero trit lost)")` even though the true product `100` is within `[-121, +121]`. Across all `59,049` pairs in `[-121, +121]^2`, `352` mathematically in-range pairs throw `std::overflow_error` for this reason (`0` pairs ever produce a wrong numerical answer). Within the benchmark operand domain `[-10, +10]^2` (`441` pairs), all operands fit in 3 trits (`[-13, +13]`), so `0` intermediate shift overflows occur. Widening the internal accumulator of `Cell::operator*` is intentionally deferred so production arithmetic remains untouched during BASE-PERF-00 baseline establishment.
3. **Host-local workstation environment:**
   - Although the host is physical (`kern.hv_vmm_present = 0`), it is a passively cooled Apple M2 workstation (`MacBook Air`) with background OS activity (`load_avg ~ 4.38–4.86`) and no `pthread` thread-affinity pinning on macOS/Darwin (`PTHREAD_AFFINITY` unsupported). Therefore, this establishes a **HOST-LOCAL THROUGHPUT BASELINE**, not a locked datacenter **REFERENCE-HARDWARE BASELINE**.

---

## Dispositions

- **NUMERICAL CORRECTNESS:** `PASS`
- **MEASUREMENT ACCOUNTING:** `PASS`
- **HOST-LOCAL THROUGHPUT BASELINE:** `ESTABLISHED`
- **REFERENCE-HARDWARE BASELINE:** `NOT ESTABLISHED`
- **BINARY COMPARATIVE ADVANTAGE:** `NOT EVALUATED`

## Summary

Resolves the five substantive findings from the independent Codex review (`CORRECTIONS REQUIRED`) of **RFC-00E1** and the SCG-08 Gate 1 evaluation harness on baseline `d3a6cf55517a3098d7bae91b07c72694bc3472da`, without altering historical experimental evidence or retrospectively changing scientific acceptance criteria.

- **Baseline SHA:** `d3a6cf55517a3098d7bae91b07c72694bc3472da`
- **Head SHA:** `5bfc0e2b7f531c4cdeca53ed9e1172f551683da6`

## Finding-to-File Correction Matrix

| Finding | Priority | Files Modified | Corrective Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **P1 — Oracle validation** | P1 | `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/exact_oracle_adapter.hpp`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/tier2_work_harness.hpp`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/test_exp_scg08_01.cpp`, `spec/rfcs/RFC-00E1-balanced-ternary-multi-precision-arithmetic-contract.md` | Enforced all 5 `OracleValidationReport` dimensions (`numerical_equality`, `overflow_classification`, `canonical_digits`, `sign_handling`, `absence_of_truncation`), exercised `oracle_rep.all_passed()` as an active fail-closed acceptance gate across all 5 bands, and added deterministic negative tests corrupting each of the 5 dimensions (proving `!rep.all_passed()` and subprocess exit code 1). |
| **P1 — Operation-accounting consistency** | P1 | `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/tier2_work_harness.hpp`, `spec/rfcs/RFC-00E1-balanced-ternary-multi-precision-arithmetic-contract.md`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/GATE1_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` | Defined explicit kernel instrumentation boundaries vs. representation conversion, normalization, and memory/copy operations; listed exclusions from $W_{\text{ops}}$; documented multiplication weight $3$ as a stipulated modeling choice rather than an empirically universal hardware cost; removed claims that $W_{\text{ops}}$ is an unbiased measure of total computational work. |
| **P1 — Counter correctness** | P1 | `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/tier2_work_harness.hpp`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/test_exp_scg08_01.cpp`, `spec/rfcs/RFC-00E1-balanced-ternary-multi-precision-arithmetic-contract.md`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/GATE1_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` | Reconciled `add_ternary()` (`c1 + c2` carry-out summation and extension-limb copy exclusion) and `add_binary()` (`a + b + carry` two-step addition, two carry conditional evaluations per input limb, and extension-limb copy exclusion). Verified against independently derived closed-form formulas across all 5 bands and dedicated single-limb/multi-limb exact-count tests. |
| **P1 — Ternary conversion costs** | P1 | `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/tier2_work_harness.hpp`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/test_exp_scg08_01.cpp`, `spec/rfcs/RFC-00E1-balanced-ternary-multi-precision-arithmetic-contract.md`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/GATE1_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` | Added separate non-aggregating diagnostic counters (`conv_limb_unpacks`, `conv_limb_repacks`, `conv_tryte_decodes`, `conv_tryte_encodes`) for `to_trits()`, `from_trits_window()`, and `from_trits()` outside $W_{\text{ops}}$. |
| **P2 — Binary multiplication** | P2 | `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/tier2_work_harness.hpp`, `spec/rfcs/RFC-00E1-balanced-ternary-multi-precision-arithmetic-contract.md`, `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/GATE1_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` | Reconciled `mul64()` documentation and RFC §3.2 with source (`4` primitive $32 \times 32 \to 64$ multiplications and `4` helper 64-bit additions inside `mul64()`, plus `4` caller accumulator additions in `mul_binary()`). |

## Scientific Constraints Verification

1. Historical raw evidence (`experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/results/gate1_evidence_record.json`), observations, cumulative trial count (`179 / 1000`), and source provenance are preserved untouched.
2. Preregistered thresholds and historical $W_{\text{ops}}$ records are untouched.
3. Distinct H02 evaluation models (timing, elementary operations-per-bit, and weighted $W_{\text{ops}}$) are preserved.
4. Validated accumulator-width table across $B \in \{64, 128, 256, 512, 1024\}$ is unchanged.
5. The 38 named-table-lookup count per `T81Limb27::addc()` call is preserved with explicit disclosure of excluded internal mechanics.
6. `RFC-00E1` remains `draft`.
7. Formal Gate 1 acceptance remains `WITHHELD`.
8. Gate 2 remains `STRICT NO-GO`.
9. No benchmarks, large-scale sampling, hardware performance measurements, or production arithmetic (`include/t81/types/T81Limb.hpp`) changes were performed.

reviews.body:
Independent review of PR #779 head `5bfc0e2b7f531c4cdeca53ed9e1172f551683da6` against base `d3a6cf55517a3098d7bae91b07c72694bc3472da`: **CORRECTIONS REQUIRED**.

Three narrowly scoped findings remain:

1. **P1 — unsafe malformed-tryte verification order.** In `test_exp_scg08_01.cpp`, `t_sum.to_trits()` and `t_prod.to_trits()` execute **before** `evaluate_oracle_validation_report()` can check `has_canonical_trytes()`. `to_trits()` passes stored limbs into table-indexed decoding; injected tryte `+14` can access beyond `TRYTE_TO_TRITS` before the fail-closed oracle rejection. Independent reviewer reproduced an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow. Correct with a raw-storage canonicality guard **before any table-indexed decoding or multiplication on potentially malformed stored limbs**, and ensure the actual corrupted-object path is exercised by an isolated subprocess negative test under `-DNDEBUG` and ASan. An unconditional guard in `to_trits()` or at its first unsafe call site needs explicit validation and bounded failure behavior.

2. **P2 — conversion diagnostic undercounts unit-limb construction.** `mul_ternary()` calls `to_trits()` twice; each invocation constructs a `unit_limb` via `from_trits_window()`. Therefore `conv_limb_repacks` must be `OutLimbs + 2` per stated definition, rather than `OutLimbs`, unless the counter is explicitly narrowed. `conv_tryte_encodes` already includes the corresponding 18 encodes. Reconcile instrumentation, the RFC definition, implementation report, and independently calculated exact-count tests.

3. **P2 — multiplication lower bound does not match prospective RFC.** RFC §4 specifies minimum full signed product `-2^(B-1)(2^(B-1)-1)` for operands in `[-2^(B-1), 2^(B-1)-1]`. `evaluate_oracle_validation_report()` currently checks the looser `-2^(2B-2)`. Use the exact lower bound or explicitly revise the prospective contract with a sound justification; add a targeted negative classification case. Do not modify the historical evidence artifact.

The other original review categories were accepted: explicit W_ops proxy boundaries, corrected primitive counters, and `mul64()` 4 helper + 4 caller additions. Width tables and 38 named table lookups remain correct. Historical artifact blob `00731bd34cfad475acde588085827698627ec60d` must stay unchanged. The independent reviewer reported 3/3 bounded SCG-08 CTests and 94 schema negatives passing, but these do not resolve the unsafe decode. No new benchmark campaigns.

**Acceptance condition:** targeted fail-closed malformed-storage path, correct diagnostic counting, exact overflow bound, source-specific deterministic and sanitizer evidence, and independent second review. Keep this PR draft/unmerged. RFC-00E1 DRAFT; Gate 1 acceptance WITHHELD; Gate 2 STRICT NO-GO. Do not touch CI, governance, or historical raw records.

records.title: Expose architecture visualization dataset provenance and distinguish Git failures
records.head: 069f285acc3307f9fe99b6d0eb706ab4f63e9840
records.body:
The architecture dashboard previously obscured the distinct historical baselines behind its datasets. This candidate exposes recorded baselines, timestamps, scopes, and missing metadata across all 13 required datasets without changing historical research evidence.

Changes:
- Add a per-dataset provenance inventory in the validator and dashboard; derive displayed baseline identities and inventory counts from loaded metadata.
- Label offline snapshots and distinguish recorded timestamps and missing metadata from current local repository or GitHub state, which the dashboard does not independently know.
- Escape dataset-controlled text at HTML insertion points and keep test screenshots in temporary output.
- Test IDENTICAL, ANCESTOR, DIVERGENT, and UNAVAILABLE using a deterministic local Git graph.
- Correct Git failure classification: only merge-base exit 1 means DIVERGENT; unexpected Git errors and separate rev-list count failures mean UNAVAILABLE. Preserve the return contract: ANCESTOR includes an integer count. Seven mocked regression cases cover failures.

Validation already executed locally on macOS ARM64 (Python 3.14.3, pytest 9.2.0):
- `python3 scripts/ci/validate_architecture_visualization.py --drift-check`: PASS, zero drift; rerun after the corrective commit's changes with the same result.
- `python3 -O scripts/ci/validate_architecture_visualization.py --drift-check`: PASS, zero drift on implementation commit ef2156d110ee0e9ea67b0cb04944fc181ccf2b7d; not rerun after the corrective change.
- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ci/test_architecture_engineering_diagnostics.py -q`: 28 passed on the implementation candidate; 35 passed after the corrective change.
- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ci/test_architecture_visualization.py -q`: 14 passed on the implementation candidate; not rerun after the corrective change.
- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ci/test_architecture_dashboard.py -q`: 3 passed on the implementation candidate, including injected-HTML text rendering. Initial sandboxed run: 2 passed, 1 failed because macOS denied Chromium Mach-service registration; the same command passed outside that sandbox. Not rerun after the validator-only correction.

+## 3. Semantic Analyzer Correctness & Scope Stability Assessment

+### 3.1 Pointer Stability vs Defensive Container Improvement
+PR #771 modified `SemanticAnalyzer` in `include/t81/frontend/semantic_analyzer.hpp`:
+```cpp
+<<<<<<< PREVIOUS
+  using Scope = std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>;
+  std::vector<Scope> _scopes;
+=======
+  using Scope = std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>;
+  std::deque<Scope> _scopes;
+>>>>>>> INTEGRATED
+```
+- **Heap Node Stability in `std::unordered_map`:** In standard C++ library implementations, `std::unordered_map` stores key-value pairs (`SemanticSymbol`) in individually allocated bucket nodes. Growing or rehashing a hash map alters the bucket pointers, but individual element addresses remain stable. Furthermore, growing an outer container (`std::vector<Scope>`) reallocates the `Scope` objects (which are the maps themselves), but does **not** reallocate or move the heap-allocated nodes of each `unordered_map`.
+- **Enclosing Scope Container Stability:** Moving from `std::vector<Scope>` to `std::deque<Scope>` ensures that references or raw pointers to an entire `Scope` instance (`std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>&`) are never invalidated when `_scopes.emplace_back()` or `_scopes.pop_back()` is executed during deep scope entry and exit.
+- **Classification:** Because existing frontend operations did not demonstrate dangling symbol reference corruptions in test suites, this modification is accurately classified as a **defensive scope-container stability improvement** rather than the resolution of a demonstrated runtime crash.

+## 6. SCG-08 Phase 1 Gate 1 Comprehensive Audit
+
+### 6.1 Multi-Precision Arithmetic Representation & Accumulator Sizing
+Evaluated across all five signed information capacity bands $B \in \{64, 128, 256, 512, 1024\}$ bits:
+$$\mathcal{D}_{\text{signed},B} = \left[-2^{B-1}, \, 2^{B-1} - 1\right]$$
+
+The implementation in `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/` strictly conforms to the exact minimum trit requirements:
+- $B=64$: 41 op trits, 42 add trits (2 limbs), 81 mul trits (3 limbs).
+- $B=128$: 81 op trits, 82 add trits (4 limbs), 161 mul trits (6 limbs).
+- $B=256$: 162 op trits, 163 add trits (7 limbs), 323 mul trits (12 limbs).
+- $B=512$: 324 op trits, 324 add trits (12 limbs), 646 mul trits (24 limbs).
+- $B=1024$: 647 op trits, 647 add trits (24 limbs), 1292 mul trits (48 limbs).
+
+*Mathematical Note:* For $B=512$ and $B=1024$, addition does not require an additional trit because $\lceil \log_3(2^{B+1}+1) \rceil = \lceil \log_3(2^B+1) \rceil$.
+
+### 6.2 Oracle Independence & Numerical Correctness
+- `ExactBigIntOracle` (`experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/exact_oracle_adapter.hpp`) implements an independent, decoupled arbitrary-precision base-$10^9$ integer engine using `std::vector<std::uint32_t>`.
+- Multi-precision ternary trits and binary words evaluate to identical integer values in the oracle across all 5 widths.
+- Digit canonicalization ($d_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$), sign symmetry, asymmetric domain boundaries (e.g. $-2^{B-1}$ and $2^{B-1}-1$), and overflow classifications are verified fail-closed.
+
+### 6.3 Operation Accounting & Weighted Metric ($W_{\text{ops}}$)
+The frozen weighted operation metric is defined as:
+$$W_{\text{ops}} = \text{OP}_{\text{ALU\_ADD\_SUB}} + 3 \cdot \text{OP}_{\text{ALU\_MUL}} + \text{OP}_{\text{TABLE\_LOOKUP}} + \text{OP}_{\text{BRANCH\_COND}} + \text{OP}_{\text{NORM\_PASS}}$$
+- **Ternary Addition:** Each call to `T81Limb27::addc()` performs exactly 38 table lookups (9 in `ADD_TABLE`, 20 in `COMPOSITION_TABLE`, 9 in `CARRY_FROM_ZERO`).
+- **Binary Multiplication:** `mul64()` primitive accurately accounts for 4 primitive multiplications and 3 additions; accumulator additions in `mul_binary()` account for 4 additions per inner step.
+- **Normalization Costs:** Normalization passes are counted under `op_norm_pass`. Primitive normalization counters are tracked as non-aggregating diagnostic counters and do not alter $W_{\text{ops}}$.
+- **Workload Equivalence:** Ternary and binary harnesses execute identical operand pairs generated from deterministic PRNG seed `0x5C608001ULL`.
+
+### 6.4 Carry-Transition Markov Dynamics
+- The Tier 1 Markov model (`tier1_markov_harness.hpp`) measures carry generation probability $P(\text{gen}|0)$, carry occupation $f_{\text{occ}}$, and mean carry run length.
+- Empirical smoke tests confirm balanced ternary significantly reduces carry run lengths compared to binary addition (e.g. mean run length $\approx 1.61$ trits vs $\approx 3.13$ bits in smoke trials).

+## 3. Semantic Analyzer Correctness & Scope Stability Assessment
+
+### 3.1 Pointer Stability vs Defensive Container Improvement
+PR #771 modified `SemanticAnalyzer` in `include/t81/frontend/semantic_analyzer.hpp`:
+```cpp
+<<<<<<< PREVIOUS
+  using Scope = std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>;
+  std::vector<Scope> _scopes;
+=======
+  using Scope = std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>;
+  std::deque<Scope> _scopes;
+>>>>>>> INTEGRATED
+```
+- **Heap Node Stability in `std::unordered_map`:** In standard C++ library implementations, `std::unordered_map` stores key-value pairs (`SemanticSymbol`) in individually allocated bucket nodes. Growing or rehashing a hash map alters the bucket pointers, but individual element addresses remain stable. Furthermore, growing an outer container (`std::vector<Scope>`) reallocates the `Scope` objects (which are the maps themselves), but does **not** reallocate or move the heap-allocated nodes of each `unordered_map`.
+- **Enclosing Scope Container Stability:** Moving from `std::vector<Scope>` to `std::deque<Scope>` ensures that references or raw pointers to an entire `Scope` instance (`std::unordered_map<std::string, SemanticSymbol>&`) are never invalidated when `_scopes.emplace_back()` or `_scopes.pop_back()` is executed during deep scope entry and exit.
+- **Classification:** Because existing frontend operations did not demonstrate dangling symbol reference corruptions in test suites, this modification is accurately classified as a **defensive scope-container stability improvement** rather than the resolution of a demonstrated runtime crash.
+
+### 3.2 Regression Verification & Test Coverage

+1. Symbol address stability across 256 nested scopes.
+2. 100 levels of nested lexical block statement traversal.
+3. Function declarations (`FunctionStmt`) and recursive function invocations (`RecurseStmt`).
+4. Diagnostic preservation and parameter count error validation.
+5. Release-mode assertion activity.

+## 6. SCG-08 Phase 1 Gate 1 Comprehensive Audit
+
+### 6.1 Multi-Precision Arithmetic Representation & Accumulator Sizing
+Evaluated across all five signed information capacity bands $B \in \{64, 128, 256, 512, 1024\}$ bits:
+$$\mathcal{D}_{\text{signed},B} = \left[-2^{B-1}, \, 2^{B-1} - 1\right]$$
+
+The implementation in `experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/` strictly conforms to the exact minimum trit requirements:
+- $B=64$: 41 op trits, 42 add trits (2 limbs), 81 mul trits (3 limbs).
+- $B=128$: 81 op trits, 82 add trits (4 limbs), 161 mul trits (6 limbs).
+- $B=256$: 162 op trits, 163 add trits (7 limbs), 323 mul trits (12 limbs).
+- $B=512$: 324 op trits, 324 add trits (12 limbs), 646 mul trits (24 limbs).
+- $B=1024$: 647 op trits, 647 add trits (24 limbs), 1292 mul trits (48 limbs).
+
+*Mathematical Note:* For $B=512$ and $B=1024$, addition does not require an additional trit because $\lceil \log_3(2^{B+1}+1) \rceil = \lceil \log_3(2^B+1) \rceil$.
+
+### 6.2 Oracle Independence & Numerical Correctness
+- `ExactBigIntOracle` (`experiments/scg08_arithmetic_work/exact_oracle_adapter.hpp`) implements an independent, decoupled arbitrary-precision base-$10^9$ integer engine using `std::vector<std::uint32_t>`.
+- Multi-precision ternary trits and binary words evaluate to identical integer values in the oracle across all 5 widths.
+- Digit canonicalization ($d_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$), sign symmetry, asymmetric domain boundaries (e.g. $-2^{B-1}$ and $2^{B-1}-1$), and overflow classifications are verified fail-closed.
+
+### 6.3 Operation Accounting & Weighted Metric ($W_{\text{ops}}$)
+The frozen weighted operation metric is defined as:
+$$W_{\text{ops}} = \text{OP}_{\text{ALU\_ADD\_SUB}} + 3 \cdot \text{OP}_{\text{ALU\_MUL}} + \text{OP}_{\text{TABLE\_LOOKUP}} + \text{OP}_{\text{BRANCH\_COND}} + \text{OP}_{\text{NORM\_PASS}}$$
+- **Ternary Addition:** Each call to `T81Limb27::addc()` performs exactly 38 table lookups (9 in `ADD_TABLE`, 20 in `COMPOSITION_TABLE`, 9 in `CARRY_FROM_ZERO`).
+- **Binary Multiplication:** `mul64()` primitive accurately accounts for 4 primitive multiplications and 3 additions; accumulator additions in `mul_binary()` account for 4 additions per inner step.
+- **Normalization Costs:** Normalization passes are counted under `op_norm_pass`. Primitive normalization counters are tracked as non-aggregating diagnostic counters and do not alter $W_{\text{ops}}$.
+- **Workload Equivalence:** Ternary and binary harnesses execute identical operand pairs generated from deterministic PRNG seed `0x5C608001ULL`.
+
+### 6.4 Carry-Transition Markov Dynamics
+- The Tier 1 Markov model (`tier1_markov_harness.hpp`) measures carry generation probability $P(\text{gen}|0)$, carry occupation $f_{\text{occ}}$, and mean carry run length.
+- Empirical smoke tests confirm balanced ternary significantly reduces carry run lengths compared to binary addition (e.g. mean run length $\approx 1.61$ trits vs $\approx 3.13$ bits in smoke trials).
+
+### 6.5 Execution Budget & Gate Separation
+- `TrialBudgetEnforcer` strictly enforces a ceiling of $\le 1,000$ cumulative trials.
+- Smoke verification recorded 179 trials, well within the ceiling. Deliberate overflow triggers fail-closed termination.
+- Gate 2 benchmarking remains **STRICTLY WITHHELD / NO-GO**.
+
+### 6.6 Evidence Schema & Negative Tests
+The schema validation tool `scripts/ci/validate_scg08_gate1_evidence.py` verified `gate1_evidence_record.json` against `evidence_schema.json`. Running `--test-negative` executed all 12 negative test cases:
+1. Null `head_sha` fail-closed rejection.
+2. Short `head_sha` fail-closed rejection.
+3. Malformed timestamp rejection.
+4. Incorrect specification version rejection.
+5. Trial budget ceiling overflow rejection ($1001 > 1000$).
+6. `budget_enforced_fail_closed` false rejection.
+7. Missing evaluated band rejection.
+8. Mismatched $W_{\text{ops}}$ weighted sum rejection.
+9. Missing primitive counter rejection.
+10. Non-numeric field type rejection.
+11. `all_dimensions_passed` false rejection.
+12. Incomplete oracle dimensions list rejection.

records.body:
Reconciles this existing draft onto latest #766 head `a763ab6876bf07b8ae7c529656cdd2e5d9cf3766`. Final head: `bd77c00122ff9cc63097d0ee2cd88895266878cc`; its sole parent is that exact #766 head. Main remains `36b3849aa1e6297e88de2ec1655777793ab0b59e`. Previous #767 head `5537fb79863009626e7c0d5c3711f826cb578af6` and #766 diverged at `755f1e60b4f9076ef3d29ac40f0206f2097b6028`.

Only `scripts/ci/validate_scg08_gate1_evidence.py` differs from #766 (175 additions, 11 deletions). Retains #766's null/non-string publication-SHA guard and two tests; removes this draft's duplicate null test. The additional publication-SHA behavior is full-string matching. Arithmetic, evidence JSON/schema, authorization and Gate 2 status are unchanged relative to #766.

Remaining justified corrections:
- Calendar validation, full-string SHA matching, finite declared numeric values, recursive nested schema types and supplied-schema pattern checks.
- Reject nonstandard NaN/Infinity tokens and float overflow in JSON-file input, including uninterpreted extra properties.
- Fail explicitly on unsupported schema keywords; restrict support to this schema's types, string enums, required/properties/items, current ASCII-compatible patterns and boolean additionalProperties. Success output no longer claims unrestricted schema conformance.
- Negative tests require intended exit 1; unexpected exceptions propagate.
- Separate `--test-json-files` mode exercises actual temporary evidence/schema files and child CLI processes, independent of in-memory fixtures.

Validation actually executed on final head, macOS 26.5.2 ARM64 / Python 3.14.3:
- Positive evidence validation PASS.
- 29 in-memory negative fixtures PASS normally and under Python -O.
- 19 separate JSON-file cases PASS normally and under Python -O (14 evidence/control cases + five malformed/unsupported schema cases); intended exit/error path required, no traceback accepted.
- Both applicable registered schema CTests PASS (2/2).
- Additional 15 nested-type/SHA/calendar rejection probes, four positive controls, explicit pattern interpretation and unexpected-exception propagation PASS normally/-O.
- py_compile, tabnanny and git diff --check PASS. Repository clang-format workflow has zero applicable C/C++ files in this delta; no Python formatter is configured there.
- No arithmetic smoke, benchmark or Gate 2 execution was run for this reconciliation.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for the table lookups inside each limb addition**

Every ternary addition undercounts table work here: `T81Limb27::addc()` in `include/t81/types/T81Limb.hpp` performs 9 `ADD_TABLE` lookups, 20 `COMPOSITION_TABLE` lookups (8 + 7 + 5), and 9 `CARRY_FROM_ZERO` lookups, but this records only 9. The carry-in addition repeats the same undercount. Consequently, `W_ops` cannot represent the executed arithmetic work and systematically understates the ternary addition cost. Reconcile these counters with the called implementation and test exact counts rather than only requiring a positive total.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count conditional checks before taking the zero-skip path**

For zero trits, `continue` bypasses the branch-counter increment even though the conditional was evaluated. The inner `bj == 0` check has the same problem, as does the binary multiplication's outer zero-limb check. For example, multiplying an all-zero ternary operand executes `InLimbs * 27` outer zero checks but records zero conditional branches, making the weighted work depend on which branch was taken rather than how many conditions were evaluated. Increment the counters before these checks and cover zero and sparse operands with exact accounting assertions.

A repository-wide search for the schema ID and `evidence_schema` found the schema declaration and documentation but no evidence writer or validation path. records.title: fix(ci): restore supported runners and unblock portability builds
records.head: b18075ad6de93091f9aea30707ef5237d479c9d1
records.body:
CI is blocked by retired runners, incomplete Windows build inputs, toolchain errors, and insufficient job time limits. Activating the decoder's Release assertions also exposes a real third-step register overflow.

This repair:
- Moves macOS 14 lanes to macos-15 ARM64 and the macos-13 wheel lane to macos-15-intel; separates CMake cache keys and fallbacks by runner image. [Official retirement notice](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement/).
- Includes /development_tests/** in Windows sparse checkout (#641), clears the GDI ERROR macro locally, confines GIC ISB assembly to bare-metal AArch64, and corrects literal/unused-field diagnostics without changing enum values or object layout.
- Builds GTest/GMock with the selected macOS GCC compiler at pinned v1.17.0 commit `52eb8108c5bdec04579160ae17225d66034bd723`. Disables only Google Benchmark's Werror option in AVX2/ASan.
- Makes the existing controlled-AI double-to-float argument conversions explicit for MSVC /WX. Preserves the native 64-bit dimension type in six demo generators, the decoder and its Windows-enabled test; POSIX-only test files are unchanged.
- Gives KernelCallResult string/vector members explicit empty default initializers, preserving their values and layout while resolving clang-cl's missing-designated-field diagnostics.
- Uses <cstring>/std::memcpy in three DPE test helpers in place of the GCC/Clang-only builtin rejected by MSVC. Existing scenarios/checks are preserved; remaining test-file changes satisfy the format gate.
- Removes an unused static tensor-construction wrapper from BM_InferenceComparison.cpp that clang-cl rejects with /WX; all benchmark registrations and exercised calculations are unchanged.
- Includes exactly the five baseline-contract documents required by the Windows sparse checkout. Adds an explicit --docs-only checker mode for Windows because CMake excludes the POSIX integration runners there. This mode labels its result as documentation presence, makes no baseline execution/compliance claim, and cannot combine with --run-tests. Linux/macOS keep the full runner-presence check; the Linux baseline execution step and Windows native CTest suite remain enabled. Frozen contract text is unchanged.
- Replaces all 150 decoder assert predicates with the existing Release-active test helper. With these checks active, the old generator fails on the third greedy step at TWEMBED R244; the VM supports R0–R242. A generated full-vocabulary loop reuses registers while retaining ascending token order and the same row/score operations. Other probe generation is unchanged.
- Raises confirmed Linux GCC/cross-platform job limits from 40 to 60 minutes and the determinism slice from 20 to 30. The sanitizer job's confirmed 30-minute compile timeout is raised to 60 minutes. Decoder/JIT regression tests receive explicit 300/240-second bounds.

Validation on macOS ARM64, AppleClang 21, CMake 4.3:
- Eight checker regression cases pass under normal Python and -O, and the registered CTest passes 1/1. Cases retain default missing-runner/enumeration/execution failure behavior, enforce all five documents in docs-only mode, and reject combining docs-only with execution.
- Actual sparse-checkout before/after reproduction rejects all five missing documents before and passes the explicitly documentation-only check after. The normal full checker also passes against the local configured runner listing; this presence check is not an execution claim.
- Three affected DPE targets build; direct executables pass 20 + 35 + 30 checks (85 total, zero failures). All three also pass x86_64 syntax checks. Functional edits are only the copy function and required headers; unchanged tests are formatted for CI. No native MSVC pass is claimed locally.
- Decoder CTest passes 1/1 in 146.86 seconds with every original predicate preserved; the active-check test failed before the generator correction.
- Controlled-AI authorization/evidence tests pass 2/2; the uninstrumented JIT equivalence executable exits 0 in 79.351 seconds.
- Compiler probes reproduce the old demo dimension-narrowing and HAL missing-field diagnostics; all six corrected demo syntax checks and the complete HAL test translation unit pass with those diagnostic categories treated as errors.
- Six demo generators and the HAL/decoder targets build. All 12 generated model/tokenizer artifacts match their pre-change SHA-256 hashes. The HAL regression executable exits 0 with 3214 checks passed and zero failed; CTest discovers no HAL test in this local configuration, so no HAL CTest pass is claimed.
- benchmark_runner builds after the five-line wrapper deletion. ARM64 and x86_64 compiler checks pass with unused-function diagnostics treated as errors; all 19 registration statements remain identical and 80 inference cases are enumerated without running timings.
- All 25 shared benchmark translation units from the local build configuration pass an AppleClang x86_64 syntax screen with -Werror=unused-function. This uses macOS headers and does not verify Windows-only branches or MSVC.
- 21 workflows parse; 275 Bash steps pass syntax checks; all seven newly changed in-scope test/demo files pass formatting, and git diff --check passes.
- Earlier local checks passed pinned dependency/CLI/hosted-HAL builds, five CanonFS contract tests, tritwise equivalence, sparse-checkout and macro before/after reproductions, and minimal-header cross-target GIC compilation.

[Prior completed CI](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/actions/runs/42830269177) at `b5178d7c` successfully compiled the complete Windows project with both MSVC and clang-cl. Both jobs then failed the baseline-presence step because sparse checkout lacked five documents; that step also expected POSIX-only runners intentionally excluded by CMake on Windows. The other native lanes and sanitizers passed. These are bounded prior-head results, not verification of current head `b18075ad`. [Fresh CI](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/actions/runs/42838121136) is queued/running. Earlier cancelled runs are not counted as passes.

Local builds use existing Asio/Benchmark source overrides, installed pinned GTest, benchmarks ON and TUI OFF; examples were enabled for the six-generator before/after check. No full local suite, native Windows execution, release/wheel execution, or new research measurement is claimed. Cross-target GIC checks use a minimal integer header, not an SDK/link/boot test. Baseline workflow audit failures remain: seven tagged action references and qemu-boot-x86.yml's missing permissions declaration.

Draft pending current-head hosted checks and review. Base `e5c30560`; original maintainer checkout untouched. No experiment authorization, research acceptance or governance activation is implied.

+## 2. Required Technical Analysis and Specification
+
+### 2.1 Item 1: Exact §8 Process Restrictions Prohibiting the H5 Watchdog
+
+Section 8 ("Resource feasibility, risks and next gate") of accepted protocol ARCH-002-R1 defines the runtime process tree with strict exclusivity:
+
+1. **Exhaustive Role Enumeration:**
+   > "Permitted runtime tree is exactly:
+   > - L: one always-active campaign owner/accountant, holding the single monotonic deadline, sealed expected identity, resource records and verifier exit checks.
+   > - V: at most one independently implemented supervisor/verifier at a time...
+   > - W: at most one worker process at a time, with one computation thread... No concurrent oracle/candidate workers, child pools, nested workers or per-case subprocesses."
+
+2. **Prohibition of Extra Monitoring Processes:**
+   > "External metadata utilities run only with V/W absent, within the same tree/caps; live monitoring uses L's in-process OS interfaces. No extra monitoring process or unaccounted helper is permitted while the runtime tree is populated."
+
+3. **In-Process Clock Monopoly and the H5 Qualification Block:**
+   Under R1 §8, the campaign clock is held exclusively by L in userspace via `time.monotonic_ns()`. When L executes within a container or virtualized guest, guest monotonic clocks are vulnerable to host scheduling pauses, vCPU descheduling, VM suspension, or hypervisor time dilation. During a guest pause or freeze, L cannot sample its clock or observe deadline expiration. However, running a watchdog process outside L on the host system directly violates the literal R1 prohibition: *"No extra monitoring process or unaccounted helper is permitted while the runtime tree is populated."* Qualification H5 correctly found: `HOST_CLOCK_ENFORCEMENT_BLOCKED`.
+
+---
+
+### 2.2 Item 2: Bounded Exception for Host-Side Deadline Authority (Role H)
+
+To eliminate the vulnerability where a frozen guest fails to observe its own deadline breach, a bounded exception is established for **Role H (Host Deadline Authority / Watchdog)**.
+
+**Scientific Justification:**
+The intent of the §8 process restriction was to prohibit unobserved computational concurrency, hidden worker threads, or unmetered background tasks that could assist the candidate comparator or corrupt accounting. A host watchdog that:
+1. Has zero visibility into candidate or oracle data buffers,
+2. Has zero interprocess communication with candidate or verifier algorithms,
+3. Executes strictly outside the guest VM/container boundary on the physical host,
+4. Possesses purely monotonic termination capability (abort authority),
+preserves 100% of the isolation and concurrency guarantees intended by §8 while closing the catastrophic blind spot of guest clock freeze.
+
+**Role H Boundary Rules:**
+- **Instance Bound:** Exactly one Role H process per campaign, launched on the host prior to guest campaign inception.
+- **Authority Bound:** Role H has write access only to its host-side execution ledger and host-side termination signals (SIGTERM/SIGKILL to the guest VM/container process group). It has **zero read or write access** to guest memory, candidate IPC, or verification pipes.
+- **Unidirectional Enforcement:** Role H can only abort the campaign; it cannot extend, resume, pause, or alter campaign parameters.
+
+---
+
+### 2.3 Item 3: Suspend-Aware Clocks, Cryptographic Authentication, and Terminal Handshake
+
+#### 2.3.1 Suspend-Aware Platform Clocks, Matching-Rate Pairing, and Unified Sleep Detection Formula
+A standard monotonic clock (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux, `mach_absolute_time` on Darwin) pauses when the system enters ACPI S3 (suspend to RAM) or S4 (hibernate). If a host sleeps for 2 hours, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` advances by 0 seconds, allowing an overrun campaign to appear compliant.
+
+**Matching-Rate Platform Clock Pairs:**
+To ensure accurate sleep detection without false positives caused by divergent clock rate disciplining, Role H must sample matching-rate clock pairs:
+- **Linux Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_BOOTTIME})$: Monotonic time that **includes** time spent in system suspension.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_MONOTONIC})$: Monotonic time that **excludes** suspension.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* Comparing `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` against `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` introduces uncoupled rate drift because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` is subject to kernel frequency slewing (`adjtime`/NTP/PTP) whereas `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` runs off raw hardware oscillator ticks without slew. Over extended intervals, frequency drift between slewed and unslewed clocks could accumulate spurious divergence. In contrast, in the Linux kernel timekeeping subsystem, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` are driven by identical `tk_core` timekeeper state, share identical frequency multiplier/shift adjustments, and differ strictly by `tk->total_sleep_time`. Thus, when no suspension occurs:
+    $$\frac{d}{dt} T_{inclusive}(t) = \frac{d}{dt} T_{exclusive}(t)$$
+- **macOS (Darwin) Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{mach\_continuous\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **includes** system sleep time.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{mach\_absolute\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **excludes** system sleep time.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* In the XNU kernel, `mach_continuous_time` and `mach_absolute_time` are derived from the identical hardware timebase (`mach_timebase_info`), with `mach_continuous_time` adding the kernel continuous sleep offset accumulator.
+
+**Residual Adjustment Uncertainty Analysis:**
+In Linux and Darwin, neither `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nor `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` undergoes discontinuous steps (`settimeofday` step adjustments only affect `CLOCK_REALTIME`). Kernel frequency adjustments (`adjtime`, NTP phase-locked loop) are clamped to a maximum slew rate of $\pm 500\text{ ppm}$ ($\pm 0.05\%$). Because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` share the same timekeeper base, the differential adjustment error $\epsilon_{adj}(t) \equiv [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$ during continuous non-sleeping execution is mathematically bounded by kernel tick rounding ($\epsilon_{adj} < 100\text{ ns} \ll 100\text{ ms}$). Even in pathological scenarios where asymmetric disciplining occurs, maximum slewing over the entire 1,800-second campaign is bounded by:
+$$\max |\epsilon_{adj}| \le 500 \times 10^{-6} \times 1,800\text{ s} = 0.9\text{ seconds}$$
+However, since both clocks are disciplined synchronously by the exact same NTP frequency servo in `timekeeping_advance()`, the actual rate difference between `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` is identically zero ($\epsilon_{adj} = 0$). Any observed $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$) is conclusively attributable to hardware sleep/suspension and not oscillator drift or timekeeper adjustment uncertainty.
+
+**Unified Baseline-Adjusted Sleep Detection Formula:**
+At campaign launch, Role H records initial baseline timestamps: $T_{inclusive}(0)$ and $T_{exclusive}(0)$ in nanoseconds. At any subsequent sampling point $t$, Role H evaluates:
+$$\Delta_{sleep}(t) = [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$$
+
+- **Consistent Threshold:** If $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$), host sleep or deep suspension has occurred.
+- **Immediate Action:** Role H sends SIGKILL to the guest container/VM process group.
+- **Protocol Disposition:** Fails closed as `INCONCLUSIVE_RESOURCE` (Status 71); host qualification is invalidated; no success root may be formed.
+
+Total campaign elapsed time is governed strictly by the suspend-inclusive clock:
+$$\Delta T_{campaign} = T_{inclusive}(now) - T_{inclusive}(start) \le 1,800 \times 10^9\text{ ns}\quad (1,800.0\text{ seconds})$$
+
+#### 2.3.2 Independently Trusted Ed25519 Public-Key Identity
+To prevent guest manipulation of public keys or receipt forgery:
+1. **Host Asymmetric Keypair:** Prior to guest launch, Role H generates an ephemeral Ed25519 keypair: $(SK_{host}, PK_{host})$.
+2. **Key Custody:** $SK_{host}$ remains strictly within Role H host process memory, with memory locked (`mlock`) and zeroed on process exit (`explicit_bzero`). It is never exposed to the guest.
+3. **Independent Trust Anchor:** The public key $PK_{host}$ is committed directly to the pre-launch host authorization manifest (`host-authorization.json`) on the host filesystem and provided as an environment variable or read-only volume to the guest.
+4. **Independent Verifier Verification:** The external host-side acceptance verifier loads $PK_{host}$ directly from `host-authorization.json` (not from the guest directory) when validating receipts.
+
+#### 2.3.3 Terminal Handshake, Strict Operation Ordering, and Authoritative Host Deadline Timestamp
+Circularity between guest evidence sealing and host deadline certification is resolved by a strictly ordered Handshake Protocol. Every required in-budget campaign operation must conclude within the 1,800-second deadline envelope.
+
+**Strict Operation Sequencing:**
+1. **Candidate & Oracle Completion:** Guest L/V/W completes all builds, all 12 schedule families across Debug, Release, Sanitizer profiles, both oracles, negative guards, and sanitizer probes.
+2. **Draft Manifest Finalization:** Guest writes `campaign.json` manifest with observed call counts, final digests, and preliminary resource accounting.
+3. **Artifact Index & Evidence Sealing:** Guest traverses its evidence directory, generates `artifact-index.json`, flushes and fsyncs all files, computes $H_{root} = \text{SHA256}(\text{read\_bytes}(\text{artifact-index.json}))$, and writes `evidence.sha256`.
+4. **Sealing Notification:** Guest transmits sealing-complete signal to Host via IPC pipe:
+   `{"campaign_uuid": "<uuid>", "guest_sealed_root_sha256": "<hex>", "guest_elapsed_ns": <ns>}`.
+5. **Pre-Certification Invariant Check:** Role H verifies host-side invariants:
+   - Current suspend-inclusive elapsed time $T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{start\_boot\_ns} < 1,800 \times 10^9\text{ ns}$.
+   - Baseline-adjusted sleep divergence $\Delta_{sleep}(t) < 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($< 100\text{ ms}$).
+   - Continuous AC mains power retained throughout.
+   - Heartbeat sequence continuous and intact.
+6. **Receipt Signing & Durable Publication:** Role H constructs the canonical signing payload for `host-terminal-receipt.json`, signs with $SK_{host}$, writes to disk atomically via temporary file, and performs durable fsync to persistent host storage.
+7. **Terminal Acknowledgment:** Role H sends terminal ACK `{"status": "ACK", "receipt_sha256": "<hex>"}` to Guest over IPC.
+8. **Guest Process Termination:** Guest L terminates all child processes, closes file descriptors, and cleanly exits (exit code 0).
+9. **Authoritative Process Reaping & Final Host Timestamp:** Role H reaps the guest process group (`waitpid`), ensures no lingering guest processes remain, and immediately samples the **authoritative host completion timestamp**:
+   $$T_{host\_complete\_boot\_ns} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_BOOTTIME})$$
inline.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sign the completion timestamp only after it has been sampled**

The required ordering signs and durably publishes the terminal receipt at step 6, but its signed `host_complete_boot_ns` field is not sampled until step 9, after ACK and guest reaping. A conforming watchdog therefore cannot populate that field truthfully when signing. Using an earlier timestamp would also allow the receipt to certify a run whose shutdown exceeds 1,800 seconds, contrary to §2.6. Separate the pre-exit handshake acknowledgment from the final signed completion record, and define how publication of that final record fits within the deadline.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+### 2.3 Item 3: Suspend-Aware Clocks, Cryptographic Authentication, and Terminal Handshake
+
+#### 2.3.1 Suspend-Aware Platform Clocks, Matching-Rate Pairing, and Unified Sleep Detection Formula
+A standard monotonic clock (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux, `mach_absolute_time` on Darwin) pauses when the system enters ACPI S3 (suspend to RAM) or S4 (hibernate). If a host sleeps for 2 hours, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` advances by 0 seconds, allowing an overrun campaign to appear compliant.
+
+**Matching-Rate Platform Clock Pairs:**
+To ensure accurate sleep detection without false positives caused by divergent clock rate disciplining, Role H must sample matching-rate clock pairs:
+- **Linux Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_BOOTTIME})$: Monotonic time that **includes** time spent in system suspension.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_MONOTONIC})$: Monotonic time that **excludes** suspension.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* Comparing `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` against `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` introduces uncoupled rate drift because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` is subject to kernel frequency slewing (`adjtime`/NTP/PTP) whereas `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` runs off raw hardware oscillator ticks without slew. Over extended intervals, frequency drift between slewed and unslewed clocks could accumulate spurious divergence. In contrast, in the Linux kernel timekeeping subsystem, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` are driven by identical `tk_core` timekeeper state, share identical frequency multiplier/shift adjustments, and differ strictly by `tk->total_sleep_time`. Thus, when no suspension occurs:
+    $$\frac{d}{dt} T_{inclusive}(t) = \frac{d}{dt} T_{exclusive}(t)$$
+- **macOS (Darwin) Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{mach\_continuous\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **includes** system sleep time.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{mach\_absolute\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **excludes** system sleep time.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* In the XNU kernel, `mach_continuous_time` and `mach_absolute_time` are derived from the identical hardware timebase (`mach_timebase_info`), with `mach_continuous_time` adding the kernel continuous sleep offset accumulator.
+
+**Residual Adjustment Uncertainty Analysis:**
+In Linux and Darwin, neither `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nor `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` undergoes discontinuous steps (`settimeofday` step adjustments only affect `CLOCK_REALTIME`). Kernel frequency adjustments (`adjtime`, NTP phase-locked loop) are clamped to a maximum slew rate of $\pm 500\text{ ppm}$ ($\pm 0.05\%$). Because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` share the same timekeeper base, the differential adjustment error $\epsilon_{adj}(t) \equiv [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$ during continuous non-sleeping execution is mathematically bounded by kernel tick rounding ($\epsilon_{adj} < 100\text{ ns} \ll 100\text{ ms}$). Even in pathological scenarios where asymmetric disciplining occurs, maximum slewing over the entire 1,800-second campaign is bounded by:
+$$\max |\epsilon_{adj}| \le 500 \times 10^{-6} \times 1,800\text{ s} = 0.9\text{ seconds}$$
+However, since both clocks are disciplined synchronously by the exact same NTP frequency servo in `timekeeping_advance()`, the actual rate difference between `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` is identically zero ($\epsilon_{adj} = 0$). Any observed $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$) is conclusively attributable to hardware sleep/suspension and not oscillator drift or timekeeper adjustment uncertainty.
+
+**Unified Baseline-Adjusted Sleep Detection Formula:**
+At campaign launch, Role H records initial baseline timestamps: $T_{inclusive}(0)$ and $T_{exclusive}(0)$ in nanoseconds. At any subsequent sampling point $t$, Role H evaluates:
+$$\Delta_{sleep}(t) = [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$$
+
+- **Consistent Threshold:** If $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$), host sleep or deep suspension has occurred.
+- **Immediate Action:** Role H sends SIGKILL to the guest container/VM process group.
+- **Protocol Disposition:** Fails closed as `INCONCLUSIVE_RESOURCE` (Status 71); host qualification is invalidated; no success root may be formed.
+
+Total campaign elapsed time is governed strictly by the suspend-inclusive clock:
+$$\Delta T_{campaign} = T_{inclusive}(now) - T_{inclusive}(start) \le 1,800 \times 10^9\text{ ns}\quad (1,800.0\text{ seconds})$$
+

+#### 2.3.4 Cryptographic Receipt Authentication, Canonical Serialization, and Strict Payload Schema
+To ensure non-repudiation and prevent signature-wrapping or mutation attacks, receipt generation and verification must strictly follow the Ed25519 (RFC 8032 / PureEd25519) specification with deterministic canonical serialization:
+
+1. **Versioned Schema Identifier:** The receipt must declare `"schema": "t81.arch003.host-terminal-receipt.v1"`.
+2. **Signature-Field Exclusion:** The signature covers the entire canonical receipt payload with the signature field itself (`host_signature_hex`) excluded. The exact signing dictionary $D_{sign}$ consists of the 13 non-signature fields:
+   - `schema` (string: `"t81.arch003.host-terminal-receipt.v1"`)
+   - `protocol` (string: `"T81-ARCH-003-R2"`)
+   - `campaign_uuid` (string: 36-char canonical RFC 4122 UUID)
+   - `host_start_boot_ns` (integer: $0 \le n \le 2^{63}-1$)
+   - `host_sealed_boot_ns` (integer: $0 \le n \le 2^{63}-1$)
+   - `host_complete_boot_ns` (integer: $0 \le n \le 2^{63}-1$)
+   - `host_elapsed_ns` (integer: $0 \le n \le 2^{63}-1$)
+   - `max_sleep_divergence_ns` (integer: $0 \le n \le 2^{63}-1$)
+   - `power_source` (string: `"AC_MAINS"`)
+   - `guest_sealed_root_sha256` (string: 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits)
+   - `heartbeats_received` (integer: $n \ge 0$)
+   - `termination_issued` (boolean: `false`)
+   - `watchdog_peak_rss_kib` (integer: $0 \le n \le 16,384$)
+   - `host_public_key_hex` (string: 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits)
+3. **Deterministic Canonical Serialization (RFC 8785 subset):**
+   - The signing payload $M = \text{canonical}(D_{sign})$ is formatted strictly as ASCII UTF-8 bytes.
+   - All dictionary keys are sorted in strict lexicographical ASCII code-point order.
+   - Separators are compact: colon `:` between key and value, comma `,` between items, with **zero** whitespace (`separators=(',', ':')`).
+   - String values are enclosed in double quotes `"` and must not contain unescaped control characters.
+   - Integer values are formatted as standard base-10 ASCII digits without leading zeros, signs (`+`), or floating-point decimals/exponents (`.0`, `e+00`).
+   - Boolean values are literal `true` or `false`.
+   - The signing payload $M$ contains **no trailing newline**.
+4. **Signature Generation and Encoding:**
+   - The private key $SK_{host}$ signs the byte sequence $M$:
+     $$\sigma = \text{Ed25519\_Sign}(SK_{host}, M)$$
+   - The 64-byte signature is encoded as 128 lowercase hexadecimal characters and stored in `host_signature_hex`.
+5. **Strict Schema Validation & Duplicate-Key Rejection:**
+   - Parser must reject any duplicate object keys (RFC 8259 / RFC 8785 compliance).
+   - Any unrecognized or unexpected keys outside the exact 14 defined fields must fail validation immediately.
+   - Any type mismatch, uppercase hex characters, or integer out of range must fail validation immediately.

+### 2.2 Item 2: Bounded Exception for Host-Side Deadline Authority (Role H)

+To eliminate the vulnerability where a frozen guest fails to observe its own deadline breach, a bounded exception is established for **Role H (Host Deadline Authority / Watchdog)**.

+**Role H Boundary Rules:**
+- **Instance Bound:** Exactly one Role H process per campaign, launched on the host prior to guest campaign inception.
+- **Authority Bound:** Role H has write access only to its host-side execution ledger and host-side termination signals (SIGTERM/SIGKILL to the guest VM/container process group). It has **zero read or write access** to guest memory, candidate IPC, or verification pipes.

+### 2.3 Item 3: Suspend-Aware Clocks, Cryptographic Authentication, and Terminal Handshake

+#### 2.3.1 Suspend-Aware Platform Clocks, Matching-Rate Pairing, and Unified Sleep Detection Formula
+A standard monotonic clock (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux, `mach_absolute_time` on Darwin) pauses when the system enters ACPI S3 (suspend to RAM) or S4 (hibernate). If a host sleeps for 2 hours, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` advances by 0 seconds, allowing an overrun campaign to appear compliant.
+
+**Matching-Rate Platform Clock Pairs:**
+To ensure accurate sleep detection without false positives caused by divergent clock rate disciplining, Role H must sample matching-rate clock pairs:
+- **Linux Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_BOOTTIME})$: Monotonic time that **includes** time spent in system suspension.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{clock\_gettime}(\text{CLOCK\_MONOTONIC})$: Monotonic time that **excludes** suspension.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* Comparing `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` against `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` introduces uncoupled rate drift because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` is subject to kernel frequency slewing (`adjtime`/NTP/PTP) whereas `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` runs off raw hardware oscillator ticks without slew. Over extended intervals, frequency drift between slewed and unslewed clocks could accumulate spurious divergence. In contrast, in the Linux kernel timekeeping subsystem, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` are driven by identical `tk_core` timekeeper state, share identical frequency multiplier/shift adjustments, and differ strictly by `tk->total_sleep_time`. Thus, when no suspension occurs:
+    $$\frac{d}{dt} T_{inclusive}(t) = \frac{d}{dt} T_{exclusive}(t)$$
+- **macOS (Darwin) Matching-Rate Pair:**
+  - $T_{inclusive} = \text{mach\_continuous\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **includes** system sleep time.
+  - $T_{exclusive} = \text{mach\_absolute\_time}()$: Monotonic time that **excludes** system sleep time.
+  - *Rate Coupling Justification:* In the XNU kernel, `mach_continuous_time` and `mach_absolute_time` are derived from the identical hardware timebase (`mach_timebase_info`), with `mach_continuous_time` adding the kernel continuous sleep offset accumulator.
+
+**Residual Adjustment Uncertainty Analysis:**
+In Linux and Darwin, neither `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nor `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` undergoes discontinuous steps (`settimeofday` step adjustments only affect `CLOCK_REALTIME`). Kernel frequency adjustments (`adjtime`, NTP phase-locked loop) are clamped to a maximum slew rate of $\pm 500\text{ ppm}$ ($\pm 0.05\%$). Because `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` share the same timekeeper base, the differential adjustment error $\epsilon_{adj}(t) \equiv [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$ during continuous non-sleeping execution is mathematically bounded by kernel tick rounding ($\epsilon_{adj} < 100\text{ ns} \ll 100\text{ ms}$). Even in pathological scenarios where asymmetric disciplining occurs, maximum slewing over the entire 1,800-second campaign is bounded by:
+$$\max |\epsilon_{adj}| \le 500 \times 10^{-6} \times 1,800\text{ s} = 0.9\text{ seconds}$$
+However, since both clocks are disciplined synchronously by the exact same NTP frequency servo in `timekeeping_advance()`, the actual rate difference between `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` and `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` is identically zero ($\epsilon_{adj} = 0$). Any observed $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$) is conclusively attributable to hardware sleep/suspension and not oscillator drift or timekeeper adjustment uncertainty.

+**Unified Baseline-Adjusted Sleep Detection Formula:**
+At campaign launch, Role H records initial baseline timestamps: $T_{inclusive}(0)$ and $T_{exclusive}(0)$ in nanoseconds. At any subsequent sampling point $t$, Role H evaluates:
+$$\Delta_{sleep}(t) = [T_{inclusive}(t) - T_{exclusive}(t)] - [T_{inclusive}(0) - T_{exclusive}(0)]$$
+
+- **Consistent Threshold:** If $\Delta_{sleep}(t) \ge 100,000,000\text{ ns}$ ($100\text{ ms}$), host sleep or deep suspension has occurred.
+- **Immediate Action:** Role H sends SIGKILL to the guest container/VM process group.
+- **Protocol Disposition:** Fails closed as `INCONCLUSIVE_RESOURCE` (Status 71); host qualification is invalidated; no success root may be formed.

+Total campaign elapsed time is governed strictly by the suspend-inclusive clock:
+$$\Delta T_{campaign} = T_{inclusive}(now) - T_{inclusive}(start) \le 1,800 \times 10^9\text{ ns}\quad (1,800.0\text{ seconds})$$

+1. **Host Asymmetric Keypair:** Prior to guest launch, Role H generates an ephemeral Ed25519 keypair: $(SK_{host}, PK_{host})$.

+Circularity between guest evidence sealing and host deadline certification is resolved by a strictly ordered Handshake Protocol. Every required in-budget campaign operation must conclude within the 1,800-second deadline envelope.

+**Strict Operation Sequencing:**
+1. **Candidate & Oracle Completion:** Guest L/V/W completes all builds, all 12 schedule families across Debug, Release, Sanitizer profiles, both oracles, negative guards, and sanitizer probes.
+2. **Draft Manifest Finalization:** Guest writes `campaign.json` manifest with observed call counts, final digests, and preliminary resource accounting.
+3. **Artifact Index & Evidence Sealing:** Guest traverses its evidence directory, generates `artifact-index.json`, flushes and fsyncs all files, computes $H_{root} = \text{SHA256}(\text{read\_bytes}(\text{artifact-index.json}))$, and writes `evidence.sha256`.
